items.value: a target letter (H or S) on the central one of a panel of five seven-segment LED digit displays (LTS-3401LP LITE ON), the four flanking displays showing distractor letters; whole display 1.4 deg of visual angle
items.quote: facing a panel made of five digit presentation devices (Model No. LTS-3401LP LITE ON) composed of seven-segment light-emitting diodes (to ensure submillisecond accuracy) on which the response signal (the letter H or S ) was presented. The whole display subtended 1.4º of visual angle.
items.quote2: The central digit presentation device (the target) conveyed the response signal (H or S). The four other devices, flanking the target, were distractors.
items.note: The size of the whole display is given in visual angle; the size of a letter and the spacing between displays are not given.

notes: The article reports one experiment. Judgment calls: (1) 'two experimental sessions that comprised ten blocks of 64 trials' is read as ten blocks per session (640 per session, 1,280 in all); read as ten blocks over both sessions, trials and blocks halve, and both stay stated. (2) trialOrder is counted as stated from the balanced first-order trial-to-trial transitions, a stated constraint on the sequence, though randomness is not mentioned. (3) The participant exclusion (fewer than ten partial errors in a condition) applies to the correction-ratio and delta-plot analyses only; the RT and error analyses (Table 1, F(1, 15)) include all 16; the diagram ends at Analyzed (12) and says so in its documentation. (4) The ACC and SPD instructions are a within-participant manipulation, one per session in counterbalanced order, kept as the instruction setting; the two sessions are two task elements sharing one settings object, with an unstated interval. (5) The vision and consent statement describes the sample rather than a screening step, so there is no eligibility gateway; it is in the Enroll documentation. (6) The EMG recording is named in the task documentation only. (7) The trial selection keeps correct trials classed as pure-correct or partial-error; no RT cutoff is stated. The journal name is not in the article text and comes from the DOI prefix (Psychonomic Bulletin & Review); volume, issue, pages and DOI are from the PMC record's front matter.
